title: EKS control-plane Terraform module: schema migration + canary health gates
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a Terraform module and associated automation for Redwood Private control-plane (EKS) provisioning that embeds a safer schema migration path and canary-aware health gating. This module should make routine control-plane changes (eg. API server flags, KMS key rotation metadata, master IAM role updates) reversible and observable during rollout. Goals: (1) provide a default migration plan and staging cluster testing harness, (2) gate production rollouts using a canary AZ/canary-cluster pattern plus health checks, (3) expose sensible inputs for timeouts, preflight validations and automatic rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes inputs for migration strategy (schema_migration: none|plan|auto), canary_fraction, preflight_checks, and rollback_policy
Module includes a preflight plan that runs automated validations against a disposable canary cluster and returns a pass/fail summary to CI
Canary rollouts proceed by updating control-plane targets in configured subset (by AZ or cluster) and will automatically pause and roll back if health gates fail
Health gates defined: control-plane API latency, kube-apiserver error rate, node bootstrap success rate, controller-manager reconciliation errors; thresholds configurable
Module publishes rollout events to CloudWatch/EventBridge and creates a dashboard link; runbook links included in outputs
Automated integration tests simulate a failed migration and verify rollback path without disrupting primary workload namespaces
Documentation and example usage included in repo under /modules/private-controlplane/examples/canary-rollout
Security review completed and KMS usage pattern validated for customer-managed keys
implementation_notes: Prefer minimal surface for module API: keep default strict but overridable values for timeouts and gate thresholds
Use a layered design: core provisioning resources + migration hooks + rollout controller resources (Lambda/controller that sequences canary steps)
Leverage existing bootstrapper outputs (node IAM, OIDC provider) but avoid tight coupling to a single provisioning flow
Migration tasks should be expressed as idempotent steps (eg. create temp CRD, copy CRs, switch owner refs) and recorded in a migration state tag on control-plane resources
Keep state transitions logged to EventBridge for observability and auditability
Where possible implement gating logic as a small controller running in a dedicated ops namespace so rollbacks do not depend on external CI availability
rollout_plan: 1) Validate module in staging using example canary cluster (manual + CI) and exercise migration-plan=plan
2) Run the module in a single non-prod AZ cluster to test canary_fraction=0.25 and watch health gates for 2 windows
3) If gates pass, promote to canary-cluster covering 50% traffic and monitor for 1 hour
4) If still green, schedule production rollout with automatic pause points and a 30-minute manual hold before full completion
5) If any gate fails, automated rollback should run and a post-mortem created within 48 hours
test_plan: Unit tests for Terraform module validation via terratest where applicable
Integration test pipeline that spins up ephemeral EKS-lite canary clusters in CI with synthetic workloads
Chaos test that forces API server latency/jitter to validate health gate triggers and rollback handling
End-to-end smoke test that verifies EventBridge events, dashboard links, and runbook references are emitted
Security checklist tests for KMS key rotation and least-privilege IAM changes

2026-03-06 Liam O'Connor: Spike completed for migration controller prototype. Found that controller should keep a local migration state CR to avoid race conditions with TF applies.
2026-03-08 SRE Review (Priya Desai): Suggested adding node bootstrap success as a health gate and increasing default canary window from 10m to 30m for EKS control-plane changes.
2026-03-10 Security Review kickoff: Need to validate KMS key usage with compliance team; blocked until key policy template signed off.
2026-03-11 Engineering sync: Decided to implement gating controller as opt-in (enabled by enable_canary_controller flag) to avoid adding cluster-side components for small customers.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Implemented initial module scaffolding and example; pushed prototype PR and added terratest skeleton. Manual verification steps documented in artifacts.
